name: Ranitidine
route_note: Oral tablets or syrup once or twice daily; injection (formerly)
owner: Withdrawn in the US and EU (2020); generics remain in some countries

discovery.by: John Bradshaw and colleagues at Allen & Hanburys (Glaxo), under David Jack
discovery.note: Designed with a furan ring in place of cimetidine's imidazole, giving greater potency and fewer drug interactions.

rx_status: withdrawn from US and EU markets (2020); OTC/prescription elsewhere
tagline: Former blockbuster H2 blocker withdrawn in 2020 over NDMA contamination
summary: Ranitidine is an H2-receptor antagonist that reduces gastric acid secretion. As Zantac it was the world's best-selling medicine in the 1980s, but it was withdrawn from the US and European markets in 2020 after the probable carcinogen NDMA was found to form in the product.
mechanism: Histamine released from enterochromaffin-like cells stimulates H2 receptors on parietal cells, raising cAMP and activating the proton pump. Ranitidine competitively blocks the H2 receptor, reducing basal, nocturnal and food-stimulated acid secretion.
It suppresses acid less completely than proton pump inhibitors. Unlike cimetidine it has little effect on cytochrome P450 enzymes or androgen receptors.
uses: Prevention of stress ulcers and aspiration pneumonitis (historical)

history.title: UK launch
history.detail: Zantac is launched in the United Kingdom.

history.title: Best-selling drug
history.detail: By 1988 Zantac is the world's best-selling prescription medicine.

history.title: OTC
history.detail: FDA approves Zantac 75 for non-prescription use.

history.title: NDMA detected
history.detail: Testing finds N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) in ranitidine products; recalls begin worldwide.

history.title: Withdrawal
history.detail: In April FDA requests removal of all ranitidine from the US market, and EMA recommends suspension in the EU.

history.title: Brand repurposed
history.detail: The Zantac 360 brand is relaunched in the US containing famotidine.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic (minor), to N-oxide, S-oxide and desmethyl metabolites
pk.excretion: Urine (~30% of oral dose unchanged; ~70% of IV)

serious: Confusion in older or renally impaired patients

facts: Zantac was among the first drugs to exceed US$1 billion in annual sales.
NDMA levels in ranitidine were found to rise with storage time and heat.
